endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Refinement of training material, transparency material, CAPA and risk management plan as needed, based on user feedback.

commentary.bottom_line: One framework, the CHAI Responsible AI Guide, recommends refining transparency materials based on user feedback, and no study supplied tests whether such an update process keeps materials current or reduces harm. The supplied record also contains no study documenting how often transparency materials become stale in local deployment.

perspectives.view: The supplied record contains zero studies testing the practice and zero studies documenting the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The recommendation currently rests on a single framework endorsement, which reflects expert judgment rather than measured effect.

The CHAI Assurance Standards Guide frames this as a "should" and links transparency updates to training material, corrective and preventive action, and risk management plans. That framing places the practice within quality-management processes. The supplied materials identify no binding federal or state requirement, so adoption depends on voluntary framework alignment.

commentary.research_gap: No study has measured whether a formal feedback-driven update process changes the accuracy or timeliness of transparency materials, how often locally discovered limitations go undocumented, or whether updated materials change clinician or patient behavior. A useful first study would audit transparency documents at deploying sites against locally reported issues over time, comparing sites with and without a defined update process.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Whether feedback channels capture limitations that affect these groups, and whether updated materials reach them in usable language, remains unexamined.
